title: In This Town, You Can Only Say 100 Words a Day
rule: In this town, you can only say one hundred words a day.

paragraphs.text: In this town, you can only say one hundred words a day.
The number over your head counts them down. Every word, one less.
Good morning costs two. Sorry costs one, so people say it a lot. I love you costs three, so people save it for birthdays.
Words you don't use pile up. Old Mister Fox saved for forty years, then talked for a whole week straight.
So the mayor gives speeches in thumbs-ups. The baker sells bread by pointing. And our teacher says one word a day. Homework.
And me? I never talk. I have eleven thousand words saved.
My sister Mia is the opposite. She hits zero before breakfast.
Then came the talent show. Mia's act was a song, and her number said zero.
She tried humming. Humming counts. She tried singing really fast. Fast words still count. She asked Dad for a few. You can't borrow words.
So I walked on stage and said the first words anyone had ever heard from me.
I sang her whole song. Then the encore. Then the encore of the encore.
When I stopped, nobody moved. They had saved their last words all day, and they spent them on one thing.
Now Mia is my manager. She doesn't need words. She just points at people, and I talk.
Like and subscribe. That's three words, and I'll pay for them.
